question: Do UP stride overrides select a different fetch destination or avoid the persistent shader readback-history obligation?

scope.sharedPath: ADD88 -> ADC48 -> AD150 or ADA38; the kept VS generation and selected variant matter.
scope.qualification: Static example, under stated conditions, of an UP path to persistent and readback history; no observed IndexedUp dominance, live resource-generation history or broader consume acceptance.

dependencies.use: Covers shared dirty selector, masked cache key, hit and busy cases, and persistent and inline guards.
Covers the exact transformation, sparse writes, template and byte identity contract.
Covers same-resource clone activation, C*(t), readback and later Original coherence.
Covers stride restoration, dirty-helper order, allocation units and geometry lifetime.
Covers mode-generated dirty 80000, local-mode variants and complete selected side effects.

currentEvidence.method: Independently SHA256-pinned exact-function generated windows of at most 200 lines, handwritten source Git objects and a 72-word serial foreground tools/run-headless.ps1 -ReadOnly query covering wrapper, stride and ADD88 links. Accepted patch-formula, clone and allocator audits were reused.
currentEvidence.identity: Supported flat SHA256 5C7A8C3AD9B6A9D39CC9BBF3DA5AB23015A568C65C723D298F846086324C4680; mapped SHA256 389EB006B1DCDE90C5DE775C92D67C18542B8FD9BD39845574206D4B213E9B13. 470 differences in 60 ranges stayed within [0x827F3F50,0x827F4280), outside cited semantic words. Handwritten title source revision 0a6cad692418431dd8bbf0b0804e8883bd4ccb7f does not establish generated-artifact provenance.
currentEvidence.entryAndStride: IndexedBuffer uses existing G30F0..30FF. IndexedUp A3568 reads entry SP+84: frame 176 and postframe slot 260, moves to r9 and calls A3048@A35AC. NonindexedUp A3000 moves entry r7 to r6 and calls A2B58@A3020. Lowerers save G30F0@A3094/A2B78, temporarily write low8(stride>>2)@A309C/A2B7C, add dirty 80000@A30B8/A2BA4 exactly when the byte differs from G2E38 and VS is nonnull, then call ADD88@A312C/A2C24. They restore the byte@A32E4/A2DDC after dirty helpers, before C588 and geometry takes. Slot, frame and stride numbers here are decimal.
currentEvidence.keyDistinction: G2E38 cached byte is a local dirty trigger, not a declaration tag. ADC48 checks Rv=VS+0x1A0*v: word Rv+28 == word VD+30 and both masked 64 stride XORs against VD+20/+28 equal 0. UP replaces byte 0, the most significant byte of the first BE64 qword; streams 1..15 stay current. A masked-off difference can request dirty but hit; equal cached byte does not prove tag equality. Hit skips patch, ID, tag, stride-record and busy work but still copies stream qwords to G2E38/+2E40.
currentEvidence.selector: No UP-specific arm forces inline. NoPS primary v=1 exactly when VS+368&20, otherwise 0; livePS selects 0. G2ABE80, linkage mismatch r27, or G2ABC80 select allocated copy. With dirty 80000, VD nonnull, VS+368&40 clear and persistent guards, ADC48@AE108 may hit or reusable-miss AD150@ADD0C. Busy primary falls to ADA38@AE13C. Effective and saved low3 mismatch plus VS bit 20 can request second ADC48 v1@AE168; busy second has no second inline fallback there. Record stamp+40 is distinct from tag+28. Restore of stream 0 does not undo persistent code and cache stores.
currentEvidence.conditionalWitness: Same effect VS that stays valid, UP stride 20 bytes and cached byte 4 produces temporary 5 and dirty 80000 before geometry allocation. With livePS, mode 4, r27=0, inline bits clear, valid VD, VS bits 20 and 40 clear, incompatible primary tag, reusable stamp and nonempty valid patch list, ADD88 -> ADC48 -> AD150 writes persistent C+word M0. Accepted same-device F808 clone shares and AddRefs that VS through Q+4 and can reach 44E8 -> 1C40 -> 62D28 -> nonnull 94480, which copies its metadata and all persistent code bytes. This is a static example under these conditions, not an observed instance.
currentEvidence.hostBoundary: CheckVertexFetchPatch uses a local UP override and effective dirtyLow; IndexedBuffer supplies none. It checks bounds and a conservative possible persistent miss without modeling r27 and stamp, so VertexFetch does not prove a particular Original writes C. Shared native_consume_dirty_vertex_fetch defaults false; base, tiled and dirty defaults and outer guards remain separate. HostPatchedVertexDigest and ReadNativeDrawShaderWords derive current draw identity and words from templates; they do not replay guest persistent history. ReadNativeDrawShaderWords requires VS+PS and vertex-only variant 1 lacks that patch model, so broader noPS classification is not host draw coverage.

replacementObligations: C*(t) includes creation bytes plus every ordered persistent sparse write from UP, IndexedBuffer and kept Originals in the same VS generation. Preserve variants, duplicate or overlapping destinations and untouched bytes. Compatible hits keep older code; busy and forced-inline writes affect only their copy. Equal pointers after reinitialization do not identify the same generation.

Current stride, G2E38 or last key cannot reconstruct history. Readback-only scoped materialize, copy and restore needs exact C*(t), preserved metadata and untouched bytes, disjoint and protected ranges, and exclusion of concurrent and reentrant observers; the copy alone needs no record, tag, stride, stamp or VD-ID stores.

Durable materialization also needs future Original cache and code coherence: stale prefix state can accept changed code and skip AD150. Maintain logical cache history and synchronize, intercept or refuse the Original boundaries that survive. SetStreamSource@FC08, which stays in place, independently reads G2E38; readback alone does not license omitting it.

Keep current-draw host template lowering, kept guest bytes, dirty-clear and staging effects and actual native draw coverage as separate obligations. A noPS native selector is insufficient to allow a host helper that requires PS.
guards: The temporary byte is low8(stride>>2):20 bytes becomes 5 and 1024 becomes 0. Allocation q=low32(count*stride)>>2 is a separate unit calculation.
Static structure can explain a possible UP dirty and persistent path; actual fallback dominance needs an ordered runtime state and generation observation, which is outside this finding.
UP restoration and geometry copy do not create a new VS allocation or discharge readback history. No runtime consume or broader dirty-fetch acceptance follows.
conclusion: UP adds a temporary stride-driven dirty request but reaches the same persistent fetch patch and variant machinery as IndexedBuffer. The per-generation ordered readback and later Original coherence requirements therefore still apply to persistent UP patches too.
